# PleaSQLarify: Visual Pragmatic Repair for Natural Language Database Querying

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#pleasqlarify)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.01795v1) · arXiv:2603.01795v1, 2 March 2026; arXiv records CHI 2026 acceptance and publisher DOI

**Reading coverage:** All 17 pages: sections 1–12, pragmatic formalization/equations, algorithm evaluation, interface design, user-study methods/results, limitations and references; rendered algorithm, performance, interface and study-result figures/table inspected.

## Research question

Users cannot steer underspecified requests when an interface hides alternative SQL interpretations and the consequences of clarification.

## Method

The system samples up to 50 syntactically valid SQL candidates, groups execution-output similarities, extracts atomic/grouped decision variables and ranks them by expected information gain. Linked visual views allow filtering, comparison and undo over this fixed candidate pool.

## Evaluation

An AMBROSIA simulation uses gold-consistent clarification choices and tracks entropy/output similarity. A separate study involves 12 SQL-familiar participants and five small filmmaking-domain tasks, with think-aloud interaction and component/usability questionnaires.

## What the results support

Clustering can reduce uncertainty in fewer idealized turns, and participants discover alternatives and use several repair workflows. Reported 84.4% task completion averages 180 subtasks and counts partial solutions as correct; seven participants missed their initial interpretation on at least one task.

## Limits and qualifications

The fixed generated pool can exclude the desired query. Execution similarity on one small database is approximate, not semantic equivalence. The interface requires SQL familiarity, and the user study does not establish benefits for nontechnical users or large databases. Changing or initially unclear intent is outside the controlled algorithm experiment.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

An interaction-design and candidate-filtering contribution with explicit coverage limitations, rather than unrestricted natural-language intent recovery.
